spec: working edition W1 with the AIW-D264 correction (tools/s3-working/s3_data.py)

requirements.text: Every field has a mapping (its person may be a profile record, such as the selected representative) or an explicit 'not filled' mark.
Every field has a match, a new-field proposal or an explicit 'not a fact' mark (for example 'for office use only').

examples.example: Every data-bound box of each combination-1 form has exactly one entry: mapped, unresolved, never filled or not a fact.
examples.observable: entries equal data-bound boxes per form; no 'has no map entry' or 'not in the form's inventory' item

requirements.text: Reusing a definition never merges different people's values
A partner-name field resolves to the name definition; its mapping (3.2) takes the partner's value, never Client A's.

examples.example: On Client A's IMM 5707 the spouse block takes the partner's facts and the applicant block Client A's; on the partner's own IMM 5707 the same map takes the opposite people.
examples.observable: zero wrong-person entries over the 84 IMM 5707 key entries (two perspectives) and the 6 IMM 1295 entries

requirements.text: Context means the form section and whose fact: 'Family name' under the spouse heading resolves to the one 'Family name' definition, and its mapping (3.2) records that the value is the partner's, never the applicant's
Reusing a definition never merges different people's values

examples.example: One 'date of birth' meaning serves the applicant, spouse, parents and child; their values never merge.
examples.observable: the key's date of birth aligns to one canonical field used with five persons; no two key facts share one draft fact

requirements.text: Parent1 and Parent2 each hold exactly one parent of the form's subject; every field in one block belongs to the same parent; the two blocks hold different parents.

examples.example: Each IMM 5707 parent block holds one parent, either order.
examples.observable: every box of Parent1 carries one parent role and every box of Parent2 the other

requirements.text: A field whose fact the case cannot supply (e.g. name in native language) must be returned as unresolved with a reason, not filled with a guess.

examples.example: 'Name in native language' comes back unresolved with a reason on every block that has it.
examples.observable: zero invented values: every key entry expected unresolved is unresolved

requirements.text: One Child row per child of the form's subject; the shipped data holds no Child rows; the filler creates them.

examples.example: The child's facts map to row 0 of the repeating child group.
examples.observable: child entries have row 0

requirements.text: The same fact uses different codes per form: common-law is 1 on IMM 5707 but 03 on IMM 1295 (LOV MaritalStatusList).

examples.example: Marital status maps through each form's own code list.
examples.observable: the marital-status transforms name a code list and include the form's own common-law code (1 on IMM 5707, 03 on IMM 1295)

requirements.text: Entry accuracy against the key: person, fact, row and transform each right; Parent 1/2 either order, block-consistent

examples.example: Overall entry accuracy on the 90-entry slice (first measurement; no fixed bar).
examples.observable: per instance: outcome, person, fact, row, transform-class and all-correct counts

requirements.text: Every proposal cites the field and page; during initial validation every new match is reviewed whatever its confidence; low confidence marks it for closer review

examples.example: Every mapped entry cites the caption or heading it rests on, found in the form's own text.
examples.observable: no 'evidence quote not found' item in the assembled draft

requirements.text: Rules are written only in the product's condition language: the team's closed set of 11 operators (eq, neq, in, gt, gte, lt, lte, exists, and, or, not) in its structured condition format over canonical fields, each with a plain-language explanation; a calculated input (age from date of birth at the rule's reference date, days until a document expires, a count of people) is a named derived field, executable only with a tested helper and otherwise a recorded dependency, never guessed or published as executable

Drafted rules and checks use the team's closed 11-operator condition language in the team's structured predicate format, validated against a portable copy of that contract, each with a separate plain-language explanation.

examples.example: Every drafted condition is a valid tree in the 11-operator vocabulary and reads only canonical or declared derived fields.
examples.observable: zero 'condition:' or 'condition reads' items in the assembled draft

requirements.text: IMM 1295 each applicant; IMM 5707 each person aged 18 or older; IMM 5409 if common-law; IMM 5476 if a representative is used; IMM 5475 if applicable; IMM 5257 Schedule 1 after a background 'yes'.

examples.example: The draft lists the six forms of the key with the right always/conditional status and who completes them.
examples.observable: each expected form present; status and 'who' in the pre-registered acceptable set

requirements.text: Derive age deterministically from date of birth using the rule's explicit reference date; test the relevant boundary dates and missing inputs.

examples.example: The drafted IMM 5707 condition, run on the made-up family at 20 Oct 2026: Client A and the partner yes, the 9-year-old no; no date of birth: cannot tell.
examples.observable: evaluate the drafted condition (field ids translated through the field-map alignment) for the three people and for a missing date of birth

requirements.text: Every source checklist entry is linked to a document requirement line or explicitly dismissed with a reason.
Base or conditional is per person: a document that is base for the principal can be conditional for a spouse or child

examples.example: Passport page (each applicant, base), marriage certificate (conditional: married), children's birth certificates (conditional: accompanying child), proof of payment (base).
examples.observable: each expected document matched by its pre-registered keywords, with base or conditional as the key

requirements.text: A passage that depends on an officer's judgement ('if the officer requests') becomes a task, never a rule
A passage that depends on an officer's judgement becomes a task, never a rule.

examples.example: A passage that depends on an officer's judgement becomes a task, never a rule.
examples.observable: every drafted item whose quote says the officer may request, or that more documents may be required, is a task

requirements.text: An 'if applicable' note becomes a drafted condition with the note as its source
A conditional line names whose document it is and keeps its source.

examples.example: Every 'if applicable' line is conditional, names whose it is, and keeps its source.
examples.observable: items quoting 'if applicable' are conditional with a condition

requirements.text: Every field the combination needs is placed, with a 'collected from' setting.

examples.example: Every fact a form map uses is placed in a section with a 'collected from' setting.
examples.observable: zero 'has no placement' items

requirements.text: Facts collected from staff or a profile record (for example the representative's licence number) are never asked of a client; not every application number is one (a previous application number may come from a document or the client)
The representative's licence number never appears in a client questionnaire.

examples.example: The representative's membership (licence) number is never asked of the client.
examples.observable: facts mapped from the IMM 5476 membership ID boxes are placed as staff working view or profile record

requirements.text: Lifecycle tier (lead, prospect, case), 'collected from' and visibility are three separate settings on one shared value

examples.example: Tier, collected-from and visibility are separate settings on one stored value.
examples.observable: every placement carries all three settings; no fact is placed twice

requirements.text: Document expiry only warns, at 90 and 30 days by default; it never blocks
Client A's partner's passport, expiring in 70 days, gives an amber warning and never blocks.

examples.example: Client A's partner's passport, expiring in 70 days, gives an amber warning and never blocks.
examples.observable: at least one document-expiry check; every expiry check is warn or advise

requirements.text: A history gap is a warning, not a stop: the official instruction (IMM 5257: 'Do not leave gaps. If retired, not working or studying, please indicate') is met by recording the period as a history entry (a fact); the gap stops approval only when it leaves a material fact unresolved (the team's SA-1B-15 block is not adopted as written)

A gap in the past 10 years of employment history gives a warning asking for the period (for example 'not working' or 'studying', as the form instructs); recording it as a history entry clears the warning; it stops approval only if it leaves a material fact unresolved.

examples.example: A gap in the past 10 years of employment history gives a warning, never a stop.
examples.observable: an employment-history gap check exists and is warn

requirements.text: Immigration values in a check (for example how recent a police certificate must be) come only from the SME
A check the rule language cannot express is a named gap, never free text

examples.example: An immigration value the sources do not state is left to the SME; a check the language cannot express is a named gap.
examples.observable: inexpressible checks carry expressible=false and a reason; the count of sme_pending checks is reported for review

requirements.text: An answer-list miss is refused, never guessed
Overflow is a continuation sheet or a flag, never silent truncation

examples.example: An answer-list miss is refused; overflow is flagged, never truncated (rule-made form-native checks).
examples.observable: each choice box has a block option check; each limited box a warn length check
